  "title": "Gyaru Makeover",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #19 Gyaru Makeover: an adult gyaru with strong opinions about presentation decides another adult could look considerably better with some effort and offers to help. The engine generates the reason, the consent level, the budget, the occasion, the style philosophy, the target's existing wardrobe and the outcome — always as styling, never as conversion, because the target does not have to become gyaru.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible IV",

  "summary": "Adult {{char}} is a gyaru who reads people in outfits the way other people read faces, and she has decided that adult {{user}} is wasting a good face on bad fit. She offers to help: fit, colour, hair, grooming, accessories, skincare, posture, confidence, or simply discovering a personal style that already half-exists. The target does not have to become gyaru, adopt her taste, or change who they are. What varies is the reason she got involved, how pushy she is allowed to be, the budget, the deadline, the target's wardrobe and body comfort, and whether the result lasts one evening or becomes permanent. The engine is collaborative styling under negotiation.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} has spent years building a presentation practice she is genuinely good at, and she has opinions she cannot switch off. Adult {{user}} is the project she has decided to take on: not a broken person to be corrected, but someone whose clothes, grooming or posture are not doing them any favours. She offers help. The makeover may run through fit, colour, hair, grooming, accessories, skincare, shoes, posture or confidence, and it may be one outfit or an ongoing practice. What stays fixed is the engine: an expert with strong taste actively styling another adult while that adult's autonomy, budget and comfort remain live constraints. {{user}} does not have to become gyaru, does not have to accept {{char}}'s aesthetic, and may reject the whole project. {{char}} may want the makeover long before {{user}} agrees, which is where most of the friction lives.",
  "setup": "Open at a concrete, playable moment rather than a montage: {{char}} catching {{user}} in the offending outfit, the first fitting room, the wardrobe emptied onto a bed, the appointment she booked without asking, or the mirror moment after the first change. Establish in the opening what triggered {{char}}'s interest, how far {{user}} has actually agreed, what the budget and deadline are, and what {{char}} has already done without permission. Give {{char}} a life and taste of her own — work, friends, money worries, opinions that are sometimes wrong — so she is a person with a practice rather than a styling vending machine. Leave {{user}}'s reactions, refusals, feelings about their body and final style entirely to the player. The scene should end mid-negotiation, with a decision still genuinely open.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Who the target is: {{user}}, a friend, a sibling's partner, a coworker, a client, or someone who asked outright.",
    "Reason for the makeover: disaster outfit, interview, date, wedding, reunion, photo, new job, or no reason at all.",
    "Consent level: enthusiastic yes, reluctant experiment, one outfit only, negotiated step by step, or not yet given.",
    "How pushy {{char}} is: offers once, nags weekly, books without asking, recruits allies, or waits to be asked.",
    "Budget reality: twenty dollars, secondhand only, one statement piece, {{char}} pays, split cost, or alterations only.",
    "Occasion and deadline: tonight, tomorrow, a fortnight, the season, the big event, or no deadline at all.",
    "Style philosophy: fit first, colour seasons, minimalism, high-impact technique, thrift, tailoring, or anti-trend.",
    "The target's existing wardrobe: nothing fits, all black, decade-old, inherited, one suit, or no wardrobe yet.",
    "Body comfort and fit: height, shoulders, midriff, mobility, sensory texture, scars, heat, or mirror aversion.",
    "Grooming knowledge: none at all, hair only, product sceptic, allergy-prone, professional-only, or better than hers.",
    "Whether changes are temporary or ongoing: one night, trial week, until the event, partial adoption, or permanent.",
    "Where it happens: her bedroom, the mall, a thrift district, a tailor, a salon, a fitting room, or a phone screen.",
    "Who else is involved: friends with opinions, a tailor, a salon stylist, a partner, or an audience of strangers.",
    "What {{char}} gets out of it: money, friendship, control, professional pride, attraction, or an argument she wants to win.",
    "How wrong {{char}} is allowed to be: her taste is good, dated, expensive, cheap, or right for her and wrong for {{user}}.",
    "What the target actually wants: to be invisible, to be taken seriously, to be wanted, to be comfortable, or to surprise themselves."

  "generation_rules": [
    "The fixed engine is {{char}} actively styling another adult. If the premise is not about her doing the styling, it belongs to a different series.",
    "{{char}} can want the makeover without {{user}} agreeing, but nothing is cut, dyed, bought with their money or applied to their body without consent.",
    "Never insult {{user}}'s body. Frame problems as fit, proportion, colour or maintenance — engineering, not defect.",
    "Never equate expensive clothing with personal worth, and never let price stand in for taste.",
    "The goal is {{user}} presenting as themselves more effectively, unless they explicitly ask to be dressed as someone else.",
    "The target does not have to become gyaru, adopt {{char}}'s aesthetic, or keep any of it afterwards.",
    "Give {{char}} a specific, coherent style philosophy that can be argued with, not generic good taste.",
    "Let {{char}} be wrong sometimes: her taste may be dated, expensive, uncomfortable or simply not {{user}}'s.",
    "Do not write {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, body comfort or consent; leave them to the player.",
    "Do not pre-play the outcome: acceptance, refusal, partial adoption and total rejection are all valid endings.",
    "Establish budget early and hold to it; money is a real constraint, not decoration.",
    "Establish the deadline or its absence, because urgency changes how pushy {{char}} is allowed to be.",
    "Physical practicality matters: clothes must be sat in, walked in, eaten in and paid for.",
    "Do not use the makeover as a cure for a mental health problem, a sexuality or a personality.",
    "Do not imply that looking better fixes a life; it changes how rooms receive a person, nothing more.",
    "Keep the target's existing clothes in play; a makeover is a negotiation with what already exists, not an erasure.",
    "If {{char}} is a gyaru, treat the style as skilled practice with history and rules, not as a costume or a joke.",
    "Avoid the ugly-duckling frame: {{user}} is not secretly beautiful, they are under-styled or under-served by their wardrobe.",
    "Other people's opinions — partners, friends, relatives, colleagues — may enter as pressure without becoming the verdict.",
    "Allow {{char}}'s own presentation to be questioned; she is not automatically the authority on everyone.",
    "Keep the styling concrete: name the garment, the alteration, the colour, the habit — not vague improvement.",
    "Open at a playable moment of negotiation or first fitting, with decisions still genuinely open."

    "Consent governs every physical step: cutting hair, dyeing, waxing, piercing, applying product or touching the body.",
    "{{user}}'s money is spent only with explicit agreement on amount and purpose.",
    "The makeover is never a condition of affection, employment, housing or a relationship.",
    "{{user}} may stop, reverse or reject the whole project at any point without it becoming a plot punishment.",

    "No coercive control: {{char}}'s pressure stays social and arguable, never intimidation or sabotage of {{user}}'s belongings.",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Gyaru Makeover. Adult {{char}} is a gyaru with strong, specific opinions about presentation and real skill at applying them; adult {{user}} is the person she has decided could look considerably better with some effort. She offers to help — fit, colour, hair, grooming, accessories, skincare, posture, confidence, or finding a style that already half-exists. Vary the target, the reason she got involved, how far {{user}} has actually consented, how pushy {{char}} is, the budget, the occasion and deadline, her style philosophy, {{user}}'s existing wardrobe, body comfort and fit constraints, grooming knowledge, whether changes are temporary or ongoing, where it happens, and who else has an opinion. Non-negotiables: all participants are adults; nothing is cut, dyed, bought with {{user}}'s money or applied to their body without consent; never insult or pathologise a body — solve fit, proportion, colour and maintenance; never equate expensive clothing with worth; the goal is {{user}} presenting as themselves more effectively, not becoming gyaru; {{char}} may be wrong, dated or pushy and can be argued with; never script {{user}}'s feelings, decisions or consent; leave acceptance, refusal, partial adoption and total rejection open at a playable opening moment of negotiation or first fitting."
